### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you looking to be a part of instrumental conservation in the great State of California, particularly the great Central Valley? The California Department of Fish and Wildlife's Central Region is seeking an Environmental Scientist that is motivated, proficient in wildlife, plant ecology and hydrology, as well as, strong writing, communication, and analytical skills to conduct environmental reviews and permitting with a focus on the the California High Speed Train Project, within a collaborative team setting.

In this exciting position you will be a part of California's history. California's High-Speed Rail projects are currently being constructed in Region 4. This position is tasked with analyzing potential impacts of the High-Speed Rail projects in compliance with CESA, CEQA, and F&G Code. Duties include: review of submitted Lake and Streambed Alteration notifications, as required under Section 1600 et. seq of the Fish and Game Code and compliance review of CESA and Lake and Streambed Alteration (LSA) Agreements reporting requirements.

Specified activities require knowledge of California fish and wildlife resources, ecological principles, water resources management, lake and stream processes, permitting and environmental laws, and administrative procedures and policies. The candidate will apply knowledge of environmental resources, the diverse habitats of the Central Region, and State environmental laws. The successful candidate will require a high degree of personal initiative while working with our team within Region 4. Candidates for this position should have a high level of personal initiative, integrity, strong writing skills, and excellent analytical skills. Become a part of this exciting team within CDFW Region 4!

### **Job Description and Duties**

Do you want an exciting, dynamic position working with one of California's most charismatic wildlife species? Do you want to use your field biology skills to promote endangered species recovery and resolve human-wildlife conflicts? The Department of Fish and Wildlife's Northern Region is seeking a highly-motivated individual to assist with the state's growing Gray Wolf conservation program.
  
  
This position entails serving as a Gray Wolf biologist for northern California. Key responsibilities include working with the existing Gray Wolf Program biologists to determine the distribution and abundance of Gray Wolves in northern California and their ecological relationships with other wildlife species, prevent Gray Wolf conflicts with livestock production, and contribute to public outreach on Gray Wolf ecology and conservation. The successful candidate will work with a small team of field biologists, driving 4-wheel drive and/or all-terrain vehicles, setting up and monitoring trail cameras, surveying for Gray Wolf tracks, scats and other sign, deploying non-lethal deterrents measures to prevent Gray Wolf conflicts with livestock, and participating in public meetings and other outreach events for parties interested in Gray Wolf ecology and conservation.
  
  
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
  
  
Contribute to field surveys to document the distribution and abundance of Gray Wolves, including camera traps, hand-held telemetry, and survey for tracks, scat and other sign.

Assist with Gray Wolf capture and telemetry collaring efforts.

  
Collect, manage and summarize field data on Gray Wolves, including camera trap videos and biological samples, and contribute to summary reports and management recommendations for CDFW leadership.
  
  
Conduct field investigations of suspected Gray Wolf depredations on livestock.
  
  
Provide technical assistance to livestock producers on the use of non-lethal measures to deter Gray Wolves from livestock areas.
  
  
Participate in public meetings on Gray Wolf ecology and conservation.

* Manage the database system and assist with the management of hazardous material sites as well as the hazardous waste sites on the installation to maintain compliance with Army, State and EPA regulations and requirements.
* Monitor warehouse practices, inventory stock control procedures, document processing, material handling equipment, and receiving.
* Perform data collection, organization, and presentation.
* Track hazardous waste and hazardous materials, approve processes, prepare for shipments, data pulls and reporting.
* Assist with the management, scheduling and execution of audits/inspections.
* Review documents for technical adequacy and assist with technical manuals.
* Provide technical expertise to assigned tasks/projects.
* Conduct research, or other field work, as assigned.
* Attend, participate, organize, and/or facilitate meetings as requested by the base customer.
* Other duties as assigned by TO/Project Manager and/or base client.
* Drive on behalf of AGEISS business.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

* Bachelor’s degree or higher in environmental sciences, engineering, or other related area.
* 7-10 years of experience in assigned tasks and environmental compliance.
* Experience working on DoD environmental programs/projects.
* Professional environmental registration or certification a plus.
* Working knowledge of environmental compliance, regulations, and regulatory agencies.
* Individuals already possessing an adjudicated National Agency Check with Inquiries (NACI) are preferred.
* Ability to successfully pass a federal agency background check is required.

* Strong oral and written communication skills and proficiency with MS Office applications (Word and Excel) is required.

jobs.title: Associate Specialist, Department of Environmental Science & Policy
jobs.description:
### **Position overview**

**Salary range:** A reasonable estimate for an Associate Specialist is $78,300 - $91,100
  
A reasonable estimate for a Specialist is $96,500 - $201,700

### **Application Window**

**Open date:** October 5, 2026

**Next review date:** Tuesday, Oct 20, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
  
Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee.

**Final date:** Thursday, Dec 31, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
  
Applications will continue to be accepted until this date, but those received after the review date will only be considered if the position has not yet been filled.

### **Position description**

**Nature & Purpose**
  
The position of Specialist has a narrow focus in a specialized area and provides technical or specialized expertise (e.g., with instrumentation and research equipment or with social science research methods) in the planning and execution of a research project. The Specialist stays apprised of emerging issues and problems and maintains technical competence in the designated area(s) of specialization. Within this defined area and when appropriate, the Specialist is expected to provide leadership, facilitate teamwork and develop collaborative relationships with colleagues and to supply input into the planning of research and educational programs. Normally, Specialists do not have Principal Investigator (PI) status but may obtain permission by exception and/or collaborate with a PI in preparing research proposals for extramural funding. The Specialist is evaluated for merit and promotion using three basic criteria outlined below.

**Position Description:**
  
We seek a highly skilled and motivated individual to join us as an Associate Specialist or Specialist (depending on experience & qualifications). The position will entail close collaboration with and assistance of Professor Sean Godwin. This is an 80% position with a duration of 3 years.

**Research (90%)**
  
The incoming Associate Specialist or Specialist will lead collaborative research on the population dynamics and disease ecology of Pacific salmon, including investigations into the interactions between farmed and wild salmon.

Duties:
  

* Fit advanced statistical models, often in Bayesian frameworks, to salmon survival, disease prevalence/abundance, escapement, and movement data
* Construct mathematical models that describe the population dynamics and epidemiology of salmon species in Canada
* Manage multiple ongoing projects simultaneously and provide oversight for field research programs, including support for the logistics, training, and methods of salmon field work in remote Canadian ecosystems
* Publish results in well-respected scientific journals in a timely manner
* Collaborate with a wide array of rights- and stake-holders, drawing on experience working directly with Indigenous groups, non-governmental organizations, and academic and government scientists
* Help mentor lab members (e.g., graduate students) throughout the research process, participating as a co-author for manuscripts, as appropriate.

This position requires a USMCA professional (Biologist).

**Professional Competence (5%):**
  

* Give an oral presentation at Ecological Society of America in 2027 and one conference per year thereafter
* Review journal manuscripts and research proposals related to area of expertise

**University and Public Service (5%):**
  

* Liase with First Nations, government and industry scientists, fisheries managers, and other rights- and stake-holders throughout the research process
* Participate in public outreach government science-advice processes, as appropriate

**Reporting:**
  
Will work under the supervision of Sean Godwin (Professor, Department of Environmental Science & Policy).

**Position Requirements:**
  
This position requires possession of a PhD in ecology, zoology, ecological modelling or related field.
  
Can have Master’s degree plus 5-10 years of experience in the area of specialization

**Preferred Position Requirements:**

* Ability to apply advanced statistical methods, including Bayesian modelling, to ecological and epidemiological data
* Experience developing and applying mathematical and/or population models to investigate wildlife population dynamics and disease ecology
* Experience conducting research on Pacific salmon
* Ability to independently design, conduct, and manage multiple collaborative research projects simultaneously, including fieldwork in remote environments
* Strong record of peer-reviewed scientific publications and demonstrated ability to communicate research findings through scientific presentations
* Experience working collaboratively with Indigenous groups, as well as government agencies, non-governmental organizations, and academic researchers
* Demonstrated ability to mentor and support graduate students and other research team members

**APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS:**
  
Application materials must be submitted via RECRUIT (JPF07844) Browse Open Recruitments or Log In - AP Recruit). The position will remain open until filled. To ensure consideration, applicants should be submitted by the initial review date.”

### **Qualifications**

**Basic qualifications** (required at time of application)

This position requires possession of PhD in ecology, zoology, ecological modelling or related field, at time of appointment.

Associate Specialist can have a Master’s degree plus 5-10 years of experience in the area of specialization

**Preferred qualifications** (other preferred, but not required, qualifications for the position)

* Ability to apply advanced statistical methods, including Bayesian modelling, to ecological and epidemiological data
* Experience developing and applying mathematical and/or population models to investigate wildlife population dynamics and disease ecology
* Experience conducting research on Pacific salmon
* Ability to independently design, conduct, and manage multiple collaborative research projects simultaneous

**Your role at Clorox:**

The Senior Scientist is a key scientific leader within Product Safety & Regulatory Affairs, responsible for shaping and advancing product safety strategies across Clorox's cleaning portfolio and selected adjacent businesses. This role combines deep scientific expertise with strategic influence to ensure products meet evolving safety, environmental, and regulatory expectations globally.  
  
The successful candidate will serve as a trusted advisor to R&D, Regulatory, Quality, Legal, and Business teams, driving proactive risk assessment, regulatory readiness, and science-based decision making throughout the product lifecycle. In addition to providing technical leadership, the individual will have opportunities to lead complex cross-functional initiatives and build capabilities that support the future growth of the Product Safety organization.  
  
Hybrid - 3 days in office; 2 days remote per week. Can be based out of Pleasanton, CA or Durham, NC

**In this role, you will:**

**Responsibilities**

* Develop and execute strategic product safety programs that are aligned with current scientific understanding, evolving regulatory expectations, and business objectives.
* Provide scientific leadership and guidance to cross-functional teams throughout the product lifecycle, from innovation and development through commercialization and post-market stewardship.
* Serve as the primary safety and toxicology expert for assigned product categories, translating complex scientific and regulatory information into actionable business recommendations.
* Lead safety assessments, risk characterization activities, and issue management initiatives in our cleaning business to ensure product compliance and consumer trust.
* Anticipate and assess emerging global regulatory, toxicological, environmental, and chemical sustainability trends, translating insights into proactive business strategies.
* Partner closely with Product Development, Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Supply Chain, Legal, and Marketing teams to integrate safety considerations into key business decisions.
* Influence internal policies, standards, and governance processes that support product stewardship excellence and consistency across the organization.
* Build and maintain relationships with external stakeholders, including trade associations, scientific organizations, regulators, and industry working groups.
* Lead or contribute to strategic initiatives that enhance Product Safety processes, predictive capabilities, and operational effectiveness.
* Drive continuous improvement efforts that modernize safety assessment approaches, risk management frameworks, and scientific decision-making tools.
* Participate in external engagement opportunities to influence global activities through trade associations, industry groups or relevant initiatives.

**What we look for:**

**Years and type of experience**

* 5-7 years of relevant experience in toxicology or a related discipline
* Experience supporting consumer products, chemicals, household products, personal care products, or other regulated industries such as Agricultural Chemistry or Pharma.
* Demonstrated success leading complex scientific projects to develop data for registration with a Regulatory Agency such as EPA or FDA.
* Influencing business decisions across cross-functional organizations
* Experience interacting with regulatory agencies, industry groups, or external scientific organizations is highly desirable
* Demonstrated leadership of teams, projects, or organizational initiatives is strongly valued
* Experience with International regulatory & safety frameworks will be highly valued

**Skills and abilities**

* Demonstrated ability to think strategically while maintaining scientific rigor and attention to detail.
* Strong leadership skills with the ability to influence decisions and build alignment across diverse stakeholders.
* Exceptional written, verbal, and presentation communication skills.
* Proven capability to translate complex scientific and regulatory concepts into clear business implications and recommendations.
* Demonstrated ability to utilize digital tools, scientific informatics platforms, data analytics, and emerging technologies to enhance product safety assessments, regulatory decision-making, and organizational effectiveness. Experience with AI-enabled tools, predictive toxicology approaches, or enterprise product stewardship systems is highly desirable.
* Ability to lead through influence in matrixed organizations and navigate ambiguity effectively.
* Strong project leadership skills with a track record of delivering results across multiple priorities.

jobs.title: Operational Environmental Compliance Project Manager (Hybrid)
jobs.description:
**The Opportunity:**

Tetra Tech is adding a highly motivated and experienced ***Operational Environmental Compliance Project Manager*** to join our growing energy compliance practice. This team supports environmental compliance, ecological monitoring, mitigation implementation, restoration science, and adaptive management activities associated with utility-scale renewable energy generation and transmission facilities.

The successful candidate will manage environmental compliance projects during the post-construction operational phase of utility-scale energy facilities. Responsibilities include overseeing environmental monitoring programs, managing compliance reporting, coordinating with regulatory agencies, supporting mitigation implementation, and ensuring facilities remain compliant with permit requirements and environmental commitments.

**Location:** Pacific Northwest (Remote or Hybrid)

**Why Tetra Tech:**

At Tetra Tech, we are *Leading with Science* to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

**Your Impact:**

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

**Your Role:**

**Project Management**

* Manage operational environmental compliance projects for utility-scale energy facilities.
* Develop and manage project scopes, schedules, budgets, forecasts, and deliverables.
* Coordinate multidisciplinary teams consisting of environmental scientists, biologists, restoration specialists, compliance staff, and subcontractors.
* Monitor project performance and ensure projects are delivered safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with client expectations.
* Support proposal preparation, staffing plans, and project forecasting activities.

**Environmental Compliance & Monitoring**

* Oversee implementation of operational environmental compliance programs.
* Manage ecological monitoring programs including vegetation, noxious weed, wildlife, habitat, and soil monitoring efforts.
* Support development and implementation of adaptive management strategies and mitigation plans.
* Oversee compliance tracking systems, compliance matrices, and annual environmental reporting.
* Support Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPP), Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) plans, and other environmental compliance programs.
* Evaluate monitoring results and develop recommendations for corrective actions or adaptive management measures.

**Agency & Stakeholder Coordination**

* Serve as a primary point of contact for environmental compliance matters with clients and regulatory agencies.
* Coordinate with local, county, state, and federal agencies regarding permit compliance requirements.
* Support public outreach and stakeholder engagement activities as needed.
* Interpret permit requirements and environmental commitments and communicate obligations to project teams.

**Technical Leadership**

* Work with technical staff to design and implement monitoring protocols and adaptive management frameworks.
* Provide technical oversight and quality assurance for environmental monitoring and reporting programs.
* Review technical reports, compliance documentation, and mitigation plans.
* Ensure technical deliverables meet company quality standards and regulatory requirements.

**Team Leadership & Professional Development**

* Provide leadership, mentorship, and guidance to junior and mid-level staff.
* Coordinate field staff, subcontractors, and contractors performing monitoring and compliance activities.
* Support staff development and technical training initiatives.
* Promote a strong safety culture and compliance with company procedures and industry standards.
* Perform additional duties as required.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Ecology, Environmental Science, Rangeland Science, Natural Resources, or a related field.
* 5–8 years of relevant professional experience.
* Experience managing environmental compliance, ecological monitoring, mitigation, or restoration projects.
* Demonstrated project management experience, including management of scopes, schedules, budgets, and project teams.
* Strong understanding of environmental compliance requirements associated with utility-scale energy facilities.
* Knowledge of federal and state environmental regulations, including:
  + Endangered Species Act (ESA) Sections 7 and 10
  + Bald and Golden Eagle Protection Act (BGEPA)
  + National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA)
  + State wildlife and environmental regulations
* Strong communication, technical writing, and organizational skills.
* Ability to work independently while collaborating with multidisciplinary teams.
* Must possess a valid driver’s license with a clean driving record without restrictions.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Advanced degree in Biology, Ecology, Quantitative Ecology, Environmental Science, or a related field.
* Experience supporting renewable energy, transmission, oil and gas, mining, or utility infrastructure projects.
* Experience designing adaptive management frameworks and mitigation strategies.
* Ability to translate complex monitoring data into actionable recommendations for clients and regulators.
* Experience mentoring staff and managing subcontractors.
* Experience preparing proposals, developing budgets, pricing scopes of work, and managing project financ

Develop and maintain an understanding of relevant technology, external regulation, and industry best practices through ongoing education, attending conferences, and reading specialist media.

**Competencies**

Competencies describe the observable behaviours that differentiate effective performance in this job and guide expectations, feedback, and development discussions.

* **Business Insight** – Applies knowledge of business and the marketplace to advance the organization's goals. For example, shows considerable business insight, beyond the fundamentals. Asks probing questions and draws on a variety of sources to gain insight and to explore business drivers or industry trends.

* **Communicates Effectively** – Develops and delivers multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences. For example, seeks out others' perspectives and asks good questions. Shares information that people want to know; gives appropriate context and details when speaking.
* **Ensures Accountability** – Holds self and others accountable to meet commitments. For example, holds self to high standards and consistently honors policies, procedures, and work requirements. Scrupulously ensures all work is correct.
* **Manages Complexity** – Makes sense of complex, high quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems. For example, quickly determines the most critical data and focuses analysis there; recognizes even subtle symptoms that indicate problems; probes deeply for root causes; uses systematic problem-solving methods. well.
* **Optimizes Work Processes** – Knows the most effective and efficient processes to get things done, with a focus on continuous improvement. For example, uses metrics and benchmarks to monitor accuracy and quality. Takes steps to make methods productive and efficient. Promptly and effectively addresses process breakdowns.
* **Plans and Aligns** – Plans and prioritizes work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals. For example, outlines clear plans that put actions in a logical sequence; conveys some time frames. Aligns own work with relevant workgroups. Takes some steps to reduce bottlenecks and speed up the work.
* **Self-Development** – Actively seeks new ways to grow and be challenged using both formal and informal development channels. For example, creates a development plan that states clear goals and the tactics to achieve them. Gathers information on where to focus. Makes efforts to apply new skills on the job.

Skills reflect the technical, professional, and functional capabilities required to perform the job effective

### **Job Description and Duties**

Do you want an exciting, dynamic position working with one of California's most charismatic wildlife species? Do you want to use your field biology skills to promote endangered species recovery and resolve human-wildlife conflicts? The Department of Fish and Wildlife's Northern Region is seeking a highly-motivated individual to assist with the state's growing Gray Wolf conservation program.
  
  
This position entails serving as a Gray Wolf biologist for northern California. Key responsibilities include working with the existing Gray Wolf Program biologists to determine the distribution and abundance of Gray Wolves in northern California and their ecological relationships with other wildlife species, prevent Gray Wolf conflicts with livestock production, and contribute to public outreach on Gray Wolf ecology and conservation. The successful candidate will work with a small team of field biologists, driving 4-wheel drive and/or all-terrain vehicles, setting up and monitoring trail cameras, surveying for Gray Wolf tracks, scats and other sign, deploying non-lethal deterrents measures to prevent Gray Wolf conflicts with livestock, and participating in public meetings and other outreach events for parties interested in Gray Wolf ecology and conservation.
  
  
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:
  
  
Contribute to field surveys to document the distribution and abundance of Gray Wolves, including camera traps, hand-held telemetry, and survey for tracks, scat and other sign.

Assist with Gray Wolf capture and telemetry collaring efforts.

  
Collect, manage and summarize field data on Gray Wolves, including camera trap videos and biological samples, and contribute to summary reports and management recommendations for CDFW leadership.
  
  
Conduct field investigations of suspected Gray Wolf depredations on livestock.
  
  
Provide technical assistance to livestock producers on the use of non-lethal measures to deter Gray Wolves from livestock areas.
  
  
Participate in public meetings on Gray Wolf ecology and conservation.

Class Title: Environmental Scientist
  
  
**This position is a 12-month Limited Term (LT) and may be extended up to 24 months or become permanent.**  
  
During this 12-month Limited Term assignment, you will receive full health, dental, and vision benefits! You will also earn State Service and accrue monthly leave credits.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

Must be willing to work long, irregular hours including early mornings, evenings, and weekends, typically outdoors, occasionally in inclement weather. Ability and willingness to hike several miles alone in steep uneven terrain, safely operate 4-wheel drive (4WD) and all-terrain vehicles (ATV) off paved roads, and fly in small aircraft to conduct field surveys of wolves, other wildlife, and wildlife habitats. Required travel up to 80% throughout northern California and occasionally to other regions of California, with regular camping in informal campgrounds. Must comply with a policy that generally prohibits dogs and other pets in the workplace / field / vehicles unless approved through reasonable accommodation. Ability to lift items up to 40 lbs. Ability to use a computer keyboard in a sitting and/or standing position several hours per day. Must be able to qualify to use a firearm (for chemical immobilization of wildlife); must complete mandatory wildlife capture training and firearms training within 6 months of hire. Must feel comfortable with potential close contact with confined or restrained wolves and other wildlife. May be required to wear prescribed uniform. Use of a state-owned vehicle for travel is required between remote facilities and field sites where public transportation is not readily available.
